slice_2_evidence_graph.note: New v2 candidate operation assurance.evidence-graph.validate performs real structural validation of an evidence-graph-snapshot.v1.schema.json population (nodes+edges supplied by the caller, target/project-scoped through the same Bridge authorization every other v2 semantic op uses): referential integrity (every edge references a node that exists), edge digest binding (an edge's declared source/target digest must match the current content_digest of the node it references), DERIVED/AGGREGATED nodes must carry a real outgoing DERIVES_FROM/AGGREGATES edge, superseded_by_node_id must be backed by a real SUPERSEDES edge from its successor, and the SUPERSEDES/DERIVES_FROM/AGGREGATES subgraph must be acyclic (DFS cycle detection). node_population_digest / edge_population_digest / graph_head_digest are computed here, never trusted from the caller. decision is NON_FINAL only when violations is empty, else HOLD with the specific violation codes -- self-validation-nonfinal throughout, matching every other v2 op in this service.

slice_2_evidence_graph.bug_found_and_fixed_during_own_test_writ: DERIVED_NODE_WITHOUT_DERIVATION_EDGE initially checked whether a DERIVED/AGGREGATED node_id appeared as an edge TARGET, but DERIVES_FROM/AGGREGATES edges point FROM the derived node TO its origin (node-2 DERIVES_FROM node-1 means node-2 is the edge source), so every legitimately-derived node was flagged as a false violation. Caught immediately by the first positive-path test (expected NON_FINAL, got HOLD) before this was ever claimed passing; fixed to check outgoing derivation edges (nodeId as source) instead of incoming.

slice_3_composition_certificate.note: Two new v2 candidate operations. assurance.composition.compute performs the real assurance-composition-snapshot.v1.schema.json rollup (computes the parent decision from real child inputs rather than validating a caller-declared one): a HARD-edge child FAIL/INVALIDATED/REVOKED forces parent FAIL, a HARD-edge child BLOCKED (with no worse sibling) forces parent BLOCKED, any child (any edge class) still HOLD/NOT_RUN/INCONCLUSIVE forces parent HOLD, and only when every HARD child is PASS/NOT_APPLICABLE_JUSTIFIED and nothing is outstanding does the parent reach PASS -- the same invariant Wave 6 already expressed structurally in the schema, now also enforced at the runtime level. assurance.certificate.issue performs real Ed25519 signing (LocalReceiptCrypto, same primitive as approval receipts) over the full assurance-certificate.v1.schema.json payload, but since no currentness verifier is wired anywhere in this codebase yet, currentness_state_at_issue is honestly UNKNOWN always -- which, per the schema's own conditional, means this path can never issue a positive PASS/PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS certificate (composition PASS still only reaches certificate HOLD; anything else reaches BLOCKED). Signing key is generated fresh per call (issuer_key_id EPHEMERAL_SELF_VALIDATION_KEY), not a trust-rooted production issuer key -- this stays a self-validation-nonfinal candidate path, same boundary Wave 4 drew around FinalCandidate/FinalApproval/FinalLock.
contract_schema: contracts/assurance-composition-snapshot.v1.schema.json (Wave 6, pre-existing, HARD-edge allOf conditional already registered)
contracts/assurance-certificate.v1.schema.json (Wave 6, pre-existing, CURRENT<=>PASS allOf conditional already registered)
tests: src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest.java (+8 tests: composition PASS/HARD-FAIL/HARD-BLOCKED/HOLD-from-any-edge-class/duplicate-subject; certificate PASS-composition-still-HOLD, non-PASS-composition-BLOCKED, real cryptographic signature verification against its own embedded public key)
bugs_found_and_fixed_during_own_test_wri: First composition test used a NOT_RUN child on a non-HARD edge expecting PASS, which is wrong per the rule itself (any child HOLD/NOT_RUN/INCONCLUSIVE forces HOLD regardless of edge class) -- fixed the test fixture, not the rule.

certificateIssue originally added issuer_public_key_der_base64/independent_verification_summary_digest/limitation_summary/exclusion_summary/target_id/tenant_id/actor_id/self_validation_nonfinal/final_claim_allowed to the output AFTER signing, so a verifier reconstructing "the certificate minus signature" got a different byte sequence than what was actually signed and verification always failed. Caught immediately by the first signature-verification test. Fixed by moving every field into the signed payload before calling sign(), so signature really is the last field added.

slice_4_revocation_offline_trust.note: assurance.revocation.issue/check give assurance-revocation-event.candidate.v2 real durable persistence (RevocationLedger.java, ExclusiveFileLock-protected, workspaceRoot/.onsure/assurance/revocations), unlike the stateless-computation operations from slices 2-3 -- issuing a revocation is a real write, and check genuinely finds what was issued, excluding any event later superseded by another (supersedes_revocation_sha256). assurance.offline-trust-bundle.evaluate computes offline_status for real from elapsed time (doc 31 SS8 degradation curve: CURRENT_WITHIN_GRACE -> REVALIDATION_DUE -> STATUS_UNCERTAIN -> BLOCKED as multiples of grace_period_seconds elapse since last_online_sync_at) instead of accepting a caller-declared status; UNTRUSTED trusted_time_evidence forces BLOCKED unconditionally since an untrusted clock cannot even certify how much time has elapsed, and LOCAL_OS_CLOCK_ONLY is rejected outright if it claims a trust_level above LOW (the schema-level conditional Wave 6 already declared, now also enforced here). Both new operations use the same real-Ed25519-signature, ephemeral-key, self-validation-nonfinal pattern as certificateIssue.
tests: src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest.java (+9 tests: revocation CLEAR before issuance, issue-then-check REVOKED, duplicate revocation_id rejected, supersession replaces the earlier event in the active check; offline bundle within-grace NON_FINAL, past-4x-grace BLOCKED, never-synced BLOCKED, UNTRUSTED time forces BLOCKED regardless of elapsed time, LOCAL_OS_CLOCK_ONLY cannot claim HIGH trust, real cryptographic signature verification)
slice_4_revocation_offline_trust.proactive_fix_from_slice_3_lesson: offlineTrustBundleEvaluate originally added target_id/decision/self_validation_nonfinal/final_claim_allowed to the output map AFTER signing, the exact same bug class caught in slice 3's certificateIssue. Caught and fixed before writing any test this time, by moving every field into the signed payload before calling sign() -- the same fix, applied proactively.

batch_3_closure.note: All 6 named Batch 3 items (Evidence Graph, invalidation/currentness, deployment identity, product composition, certificate/revocation/offline verification) now have real runtime behavior on top of the Wave 2/5/6 JSON Schema contracts Batch 1 built. "invalidation/currentness" is addressed by deployment.verify-installed's real identity comparison and the offline-trust-bundle degradation computation; a dedicated standalone CurrentnessSnapshot compute engine (Wave 5's currentness-snapshot.v1.schema.json in isolation from a deployment context) remains a real gap, noted here rather than silently claimed complete, and is natural follow-on work for a later batch/wave rather than a blocker for Batch 3's own named scope.

batches.name: Enterprise / Trust
batches.scope_note: 137 SS27 Batch 4 items: Policy Profile, industry profile, RBAC/SoD/four-eyes/delegation/break-glass, Plugin/Adapter qualification, external integration trust. Unlike Batch 3, none of these had a pre-existing Wave-built JSON Schema contract from Batch 1 -- this batch needs new contracts as well as new runtime behavior.

slice_1_policy_profile_and_sod.note: FR-COM-013 (02_FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENTS_AND_PROGRAMS.md): a regulated-industry Enterprise Edition must enforce Separation of Duties -- the same actor cannot both develop (Patch apply) and verify/accept the same ImprovementRequest; a general Plan only recommends this, it does not enforce it. New policy-profile.v1.schema.json establishes industry_class (STANDARD vs 4 REGULATED_* values) and sod_enforcement (ADVISORY vs ENFORCED) as the single switch between those two behaviors, with the schema itself forbidding STANDARD+ENFORCED (matching FR-COM-013's own wording). SeparationOfDutiesLedger.java is a durable per-improvement_request_id ledger (ExclusiveFileLock-protected): under ENFORCED, an actor who already recorded a different stage (DEVELOP/VERIFY/ACCEPT) for the same request is rejected outright (SecurityException, before anything is written) rather than merely flagged -- "모두 수행할 수 없다" means genuinely cannot, not just logged. Under ADVISORY the conflict is still recorded but not blocked, and assurance.sod.check surfaces it.
tests: src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SeparationOfDutiesLedgerTest.java (NEW, 6 tests: enforced conflict rejected + leaves no partial record, advisory conflict recorded not blocked, different actors never conflict, same actor/same stage twice is not a conflict, unrecorded request has no stages)

src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest.java (+4 tests: enforced regulated policy blocks the same actor across a real Bridge/RBAC-authenticated call; different actors under the same enforced policy both succeed and sod.check reports clean; STANDARD industry cannot declare ENFORCED; ADVISORY records and surfaces the conflict via sod.check)
slice_1_policy_profile_and_sod.known_gap_not_yet_covered: sod.record-stage is an additive v2 candidate op that a caller must choose to invoke -- it is not yet a MANDATORY gate wired directly into the real v1 patch.apply/plan.approve/git.commit dispatcher chain (those operations do not yet call this ledger themselves). That deeper integration -- and reading the actual signer identity out of each stage's approval receipt rather than trusting a caller-declared stage label -- is real follow-on work, noted here rather than silently claimed complete. four-eyes/delegation/break-glass and Plugin/Adapter qualification and external integration trust remain open Batch 4 items.

slice_2_four_eyes.note: policy-profile.v1.schema.json's four_eyes_required flag now has real enforcement. FourEyesLedger.java (durable, ExclusiveFileLock-protected, one file per approval_subject_id) only reports a subject satisfied once REQUIRED_DISTINCT_APPROVERS (2) genuinely distinct actors have each recorded an approval. The same actor approving twice is rejected outright (SecurityException) rather than silently double-counted or silently ignored -- either failure mode would defeat the entire point of a dual-control check.
tests: src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest.java (+4 tests, including a real two-distinct-authenticated-identity satisfaction case)
slice_2_four_eyes.known_gap_not_yet_covered: Same additive-not-mandatory-gate caveat as slice 1's sod.record-stage -- this is not yet wired as a required precondition inside any real v1 dispatcher operation (e.g. license.revoke, case.legal-hold) that doc 08A/04 would actually want dual control on. Delegation/break-glass, Plugin/Adapter qualification, and external integration trust remain open Batch 4 items.

slice_3_delegation_break_glass.note: Real bounded-time role delegation and emergency-override audit trail, the remaining "RBAC/SoD/four-eyes/delegation/break-glass" items. DelegationLedger.java (one file per delegation_id, matching RevocationLedger/BreakGlassLedger's proven globally-unique-ID pattern) real-expiry-checks grants at read time -- an expired grant is simply never returned by activeGrantsFor, never a caller-declared "still active" flag -- and rejects self-delegation and a delegator who does not actually hold (via server-authenticated identity.roles(), never a caller claim) the role being delegated. BreakGlassLedger.java creates every emergency-override event with review_required permanently true and review_completed false -- there is no constructor path that creates an already-reviewed event -- and rejects a reviewer who is the same actor as the invoker (the same actor cannot grant themselves emergency access and also sign off on it), mirroring the FR-COM-013 SoD principle from slice 1 applied to break-glass review.
tests: src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest.java (+4 tests: delegator-without-role rejected, successful grant found by check, invoker cannot review own break-glass event, distinct reviewer closes it)
slice_3_delegation_break_glass.bug_found_and_fixed_during_own_test_writ: DelegationLedger originally stored grants one-file-per-delegate-actor, so its delegation_id uniqueness check only scanned that one delegate's file -- two different delegates could be granted under the SAME delegation_id without either call ever seeing the other, silently breaking the "one ID identifies exactly one grant" invariant every other ledger this session relies on. Caught by the first duplicate-ID test (used a different delegate on the second call, expected rejection, got silent success). Fixed by switching to one-file-per-delegation_id (matching RevocationLedger/BreakGlassLedger's already-proven pattern) with activeGrantsFor scanning and filtering instead of a single direct file lookup.
slice_3_delegation_break_glass.known_gap_not_yet_covered: Same additive-not-mandatory-gate caveat as slices 1-2 -- delegation is not yet consulted by TenantRbacService.requireRole itself (a delegated role does not actually widen what the delegate is allowed to do at the real RBAC boundary yet). Plugin/Adapter qualification and external integration trust remain open Batch 4 items.

slice_4_plugin_adapter_qualification.note: plugin-manifest.v1.schema.json SS5 real qualification computation (Wave 7 schema, already registered): an unsigned or revoked publisher forbids qualification outright (REVOKED / NOT_QUALIFIED, real check on caller-declared publisher_signature_valid/publisher_revoked -- eventual real signature verification against a trust root is a further step, not yet wired); an undeclared privilege (a required_privileges entry with no matching access_declarations entry) blocks qualification with a specific UNDECLARED_PRIVILEGE reason rather than silently passing through; and, via PluginQualificationLedger (durable, one file per plugin_id), a plugin previously QUALIFIED whose artifact_digest has since changed drops to QUALIFICATION_PENDING instead of silently carrying the old QUALIFIED state forward onto different bytes -- the actual mechanism behind SS5's "any artifact digest change requires requalification."
tests: src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest.java (+5 tests: revoked publisher, invalid signature, undeclared privilege, full qualification, digest-change drops a QUALIFIED plugin to QUALIFICATION_PENDING)
slice_4_plugin_adapter_qualification.known_gap_not_yet_covered: publisher_signature_valid/publisher_revoked are accepted as caller-declared inputs here, not independently re-verified against a real trust-rooted publisher key registry (analogous to how deployment.install's verification_key already does real Ed25519 verification -- plugin qualification could reuse that same primitive as later follow-on work). External integration trust remains the last open Batch 4 item.

slice_5_external_integration_trust.note: 52_EXTERNAL_INTEGRATION_AND_SUPPLY_CHAIN_TRUST.md (DESIGN_ONLY/DRAFT/NON_FINAL, no JSON Schema of its own yet) SS6/SS7/SS10/SS11 real reconciliation: an external provider's state and ONSure's local state can genuinely differ, and the doc is explicit a mismatch becomes EXTERNAL_STATE_CONFLICT_HOLD -- never an automatic pick of "whichever side looks better" ("자동 좋은 쪽 선택 금지"). Implemented as real subject-identity and value comparison across the 4 provider classes doc 52 names as concrete examples (CI_STATUS, CONTAINER_DIGEST, LICENSE_STATUS, DEPENDENCY_ADVISORY): a provider subject that does not match the expected/local subject (CI status from a different commit; a mutable tag whose digest moved) is SUBJECT_MISMATCH; a matching subject with a differing value (license ACTIVE locally, REVOKED at the provider) is VALUE_MISMATCH. Just as important: a failed/timed-out provider lookup is never silently treated as a clean/zero result (doc 52's own named negative test, "advisory lookup timeout을 0 vulnerability로 처리") -- it fails closed to HOLD exactly like a genuine conflict, before the subject/value comparison ever runs.
slice_5_external_integration_trust.contract_schema: None -- doc 52 has no dedicated JSON Schema yet (its own Integration Profile object, SS2, remains design-only). This slice implements the reconciliation ALGORITHM (SS6/SS10), the most concrete and directly actionable part of the doc, rather than the full Integration Profile data model, which is real follow-on work.
tests: src/test/java/kr/co/oruda/onsure/platform/SemanticAssuranceV2DispatcherBridgeTest.java (+4 tests, each directly mapped to a doc 52 named example: failed lookup never reads clean, CI status from a different commit is a conflict not an auto-pick, license ACTIVE-cached/REVOKED-remote is a conflict, matching state is CONSISTENT)
slice_5_external_integration_trust.known_gap_not_yet_covered: The full Integration Profile object (SS2: credential mode, allowed operations, data classes, trust basis, freshness/replay policy, qualification status) and per-provider-class specific binding rules (SS3: Git/CI repository+tree binding, Package/Container SBOM+signature, AI provider model/deployment/profile tracking, Payment/OLicense entitlement-authority separation, Notification delivery-receipt vs business-acknowledgment) remain design-only and are real follow-on work, not silently claimed complete.

batch_4_closure.note: All 5 named Batch 4 items (Policy Profile, industry profile, RBAC/SoD/four-eyes/delegation/break-glass, Plugin/Adapter qualification, external integration trust) now have real, tested runtime behavior. Unlike Batch 3, most of this batch had no pre-existing Wave-built schema, so slice 1 added policy-profile.v1.schema.json; plugin-manifest.v1.schema.json (Wave 7) already existed and slice 4 built on it the same way Batch 3 built on Wave 5/6. Every slice's known-gap section names its real remaining work (mandatory-gate wiring into the real v1 dispatcher chain for SoD/four-eyes; RBAC actually consulting delegation grants; real publisher-signature verification for plugins; the full external Integration Profile data model) rather than silently claiming full closure.
